hints.title: Kleene Star Preceding Match Obstacle
hints.text: In regular expressions, '*' matches zero or more occurrences of the preceding element. How can evaluating whether to match zero preceding characters versus matching one and advancing verify string conformance?

hints.title: Kleene Star Dual Case Invariant
hints.text: When p[j - 1] == '*', match can ignore the pair (inherit from j - 2) or, if the preceding character matches s[i - 1], inherit from matching s[i - 2] with the same pattern (inherit from i - 1, j).

hints.title: 2D Boolean Table Matching Procedure
hints.text: Build a 2D boolean array of size (m + 1) x (n + 1) with (0, 0) set to true. Handle '*' on empty strings by checking j - 2. For each i in s and j in p: if p[j - 1] is '*', take table[i][j - 2], and if preceding character matches s[i - 1], or with table[i - 1][j]. Otherwise, if characters match or p[j - 1] is '.', inherit table[i - 1][j - 1]. Return table[m][n].

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Populates the 2D matching grid in quadratic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursive backtracking without memoization explores overlapping '*' sub-trees.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: 2D boolean grid provides explicit indexing for j - 2 lookback.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Carefully structuring the zero-occurrence lookup dp[i][j-2] versus one-or-more lookup dp[i-1][j].
